questionsToConsider: Which group is this about: a team, a whole organisation, a course cohort or a volunteer community?
Will you run it once, or every month or quarter so you can see the trend?
Who follows up with people who ask for a private chat, and are they someone people trust?
Should answers be anonymous apart from the email of those who ask to be contacted?
guide.howToUseResponses: Look at the average happiness score and the split between happier, same and less happy, then read the written answers from the less happy group first, since they point at what to fix. Compare the belonging grid between check-ins to see which statement is moving. Reply to every private chat request within a few days, and tell the whole group one thing you changed because of the survey before you run it again.
customizeSteps: Name the team, program or community in the greeting and the first question so nobody answers about their life in general.
Swap the options in the happiness question for the things your group actually offers, such as events, mentoring or flexible hours.
Share the link on the same day each month or quarter, so the scores stay comparable from one check-in to the next.

faqs.q: What questions should a happiness survey include?
faqs.a: A simple overall score, whether things are getting better or worse, what adds to people's happiness and one open question about what to change. This template covers all four and asks a different follow-up depending on the trend.

faqs.q: How often should you run a happiness survey?
faqs.a: Monthly or quarterly works for most groups. Often enough to catch a change early, but not so often that people stop reading the questions.

faqs.q: Should a happiness survey be anonymous?
faqs.a: Mostly, yes. People answer more honestly when they are not named. This one only asks for an email from people who want a private follow-up.

faqs.q: Can I use this happiness survey outside of work?
faqs.a: Yes. It is written for any group, such as a class, a club or a volunteer program. Change the wording in the first question to name yours.

doc.title: Happiness check-in
doc.description: A quick, honest check-in on how people feel, with a private follow-up for anyone who asks.

blocks.title: Hi! This is a quick check-in on how you're feeling here lately. It takes about three minutes, and there are no wrong answers.
Over the past month, how happy have you felt here?
blocks.description: Think about this team, program or group specifically, not life in general.

blocks.title: Compared with a few months ago, is that...
What's one recent moment that made you glad to be part of this?
What's changed for you? Anything you're comfortable sharing helps.
Which of these add most to your happiness here?

options.label: The people I spend time with
Feeling that what I do matters
Freedom to decide how I work
A manageable amount on my plate

blocks.title: How much do you agree with each of these?

rows.label: I feel like I belong here
I look forward to the time I spend here
I have energy left for the rest of my life

blocks.title: If you could change one thing to make this a happier place, what would it be?
Would you like someone to reach out for a private chat about how you're doing?
What's the best email to reach you on?
blocks.description: Only the person following up will see this.

endings.title: Thanks for checking in 😊
endings.bodyMd: We look at the answers together, not one by one, and share what we're changing because of them.

endings.title: Thank you, we'll be in touch
endings.bodyMd: Someone will email you within a few days to find a time that suits you. The conversation stays between the two of you.
